The Daily AI Brief and Emerging AI Watch prioritize primary-origin sources that can reveal papers, models, code, releases, and emerging practices early. Newsletters and aggregators remain useful for discovery and catching up, but they do not replace original evidence.

Every candidate still passes freshness, authority, evidence-quality, novelty, relevance, and duplication checks. Community discussion can identify a lead or a limitation; consequential claims must be traced to an original paper, model card, repository, official release, system card, or other authoritative evidence. Preprints and vendor-reported results are labeled for what they are.

<section class="source-channel"><h2>1. arXiv — cs.AI, cs.LG, and cs.CL</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Public monitoring</p><p>High-volume first public posting point for AI and language-model research.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Primary research lead. Verify the paper, authors, submission date, methods, limitations, and later versions; preprint status is not peer review.</p><ul><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">arXiv cs.AI recent submissions</a></li><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/list/cs.LG/recent" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">arXiv cs.LG recent submissions</a></li><li><a href="https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">arXiv cs.CL recent submissions</a></li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>2. X — verified researchers and AI labs</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Assisted review</p><p>Fast release signals, demonstrations, replication notes, and early critiques from named researchers and labs.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Discovery signal only. Confirm account identity, follow every claim to original evidence, and do not treat screenshots, engagement, or reposts as validation.</p><ul><li><a href="https://x.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">X — verified researchers and AI labs</a> · assisted review</li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>3. Hugging Face Hub and Daily Papers</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Public monitoring</p><p>Open models, datasets, demos, model cards, and community discussion often appear with or before written coverage.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Verify the uploader, license, model or dataset card, version, linked paper or repository, and independently relevant limitations. Popularity is not quality evidence.</p><ul><li><a href="https://huggingface.co/models?sort=trending" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Models</a></li><li><a href="https://huggingface.co/datasets?sort=trending" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Datasets</a></li><li><a href="https://huggingface.co/spaces?sort=trending" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Spaces</a></li><li><a href="https://huggingface.co/papers" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hugging Face Daily Papers</a></li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>4. Reddit — r/MachineLearning and r/LocalLLaMA</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Public monitoring</p><p>Early practitioner discussion, replication reports, open-model tests, local inference techniques, and practical failure reports.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Discovery and critique signal only. Distinguish direct testing from opinion or rumor; verify releases, benchmarks, and claims at their origin.</p><ul><li><a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/MachineLearning/new/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">r/MachineLearning</a></li><li><a href="https://www.reddit.com/r/LocalLLaMA/new/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">r/LocalLLaMA</a></li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>7. Hacker News</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Public monitoring</p><p>Early technical discussion of papers, releases, repositories, and new tools, often with useful implementation caveats.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Discovery and critique signal only. Trace submissions and factual claims to original evidence; comments can supply questions, not confirmation.</p><ul><li><a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/newest" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Hacker News Newest</a></li><li><a href="https://news.ycombinator.com/show" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Show HN</a></li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>8. Specialized AI Discord communities</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Assisted review</p><p>Real-time implementation discussion around research groups and model families can reveal early working examples and limitations.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Discovery signal only. Use only official or verified community access, never expose private discussion, and require public original evidence before selection.</p><ul><li><a href="https://discord.com/discovery" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Specialized AI Discord communities</a> · assisted review</li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>9. YouTube — official labs and researchers</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Assisted review</p><p>Official demonstrations, paper walkthroughs, research talks, and early technical explanations can precede written coverage.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Verify channel identity, upload date, runtime, claims, and linked original evidence. Demonstrations and commentary are not independent validation.</p><ul><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@OpenAI" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">OpenAI on YouTube</a> · assisted review</li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@anthropic-ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Anthropic on YouTube</a> · assisted review</li><li><a href="https://www.youtube.com/@googledeepmind" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Google DeepMind on YouTube</a> · assisted review</li></ul></section>
<section class="source-channel"><h2>10. AI conference sites and OpenReview</h2><p><strong>Monitoring:</strong> Public monitoring plus assisted review</p><p>Conference programs, camera-ready papers, public reviews, and author responses add scrutiny and revisions to earlier preprints.</p><p><strong>Evidence treatment:</strong> Record review stage and version. Separate accepted or camera-ready work from submissions, workshop papers, reviews, and author responses.</p><ul><li><a href="https://openreview.net/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">OpenReview</a> · assisted review</li><li><a href="https://neurips.cc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">NeurIPS</a></li><li><a href="https://icml.cc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ICML</a></li><li><a href="https://iclr.cc/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ICLR</a></li><li><a href="https://aclanthology.org/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">ACL Anthology</a></li></ul></section>

## How the two products use these sources

- **Daily AI Brief:** sources expand the candidate pool for six articles, two videos, and one podcast. Selection is never automatic merely because an item appears in a monitored channel.
- **Emerging AI Watch:** sources help identify unfamiliar concepts before they become established topics. Reader interest can trigger deeper research but cannot bypass evidence requirements.
- **Restricted channels:** X and specialized Discord communities use assisted review. Private material, inaccessible posts, engagement counts, rumors, and screenshots are not treated as verified evidence.
